A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, with MixQuant renamed PeRQ in v2. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation analyses, quantization experiments on Llama3 and Qwen3, and permutation and pipeline ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds quantization-error analysis, calibration studies, GSM8K evaluation, and SmolLM3 experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, permutation fusion, rotation placements, and the two principal pipeline variants remain unchanged. MixQuant becomes PeRQ; Figure 5's per-token permutations are a diagnostic evaluation setting.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond WikiText2 calibration and the existing five commonsense tasks by adding C4 and FineWeb calibration distributions (Table 8) and GSM8K mathematical generation (Table 10). Existing dataset and task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds a separately evaluated SpinQuant variant without permutations, using an online block rotation with b=32. Figure 5 introduces a direct MassDiff/ZigZag/identity comparison for quantization error. The original benchmark and permutation-comparison sets remain.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include per-token permutation optimization and normalized quantization-error measurement (Figure 5), an RTN block-size sweep (Table 5), 128K-token permutation calibration (Table 7), and a SmolLM3 3B configuration (Table 12). The existing main experiments retain their stated settings.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands tests of the proposed mechanism: Figure 5 links the bound to actual quantization error, Table 5 isolates permutations under RTN, and Tables 7–8 test calibration size and source sensitivity. Table 10 adds further no-permutation comparisons, although its claimed MR-Qronos control equivalence conflicts with Section 5's rotation definitions.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averaging for random permutations and mean/standard-deviation activation statistics in Figure 4. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All seven existing tables retain their numerical entries after matching renumbering. Substantial new results appear in Figure 5 and Tables 5, 7, 8, 10, and 12, including 37.5–40.5% mean quantization-error reductions and GSM8K accuracies of 57.3% and 45.9% for PeRQ* and PeRQ†. These are newly reported experiments.

T1.justification: The notation section revises the quantizer alphabet from A contained in Z with exactly 2^q elements to A contained in sZ with at most 2^q elements. The principal outlier bounds, assumptions, and Appendix D proofs remain mathematically unchanged; the computational analysis is retained in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The same three central contributions remain: non-asymptotic outlier analysis, MassDiff mass balancing, and permutation fusion without additional inference overhead. The headline 90% versus 46% recovery claim is retained; added experiments support the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations contrasting MassDiff's mass-balancing objective with ZigZag's proxy, hypotheses about calibration-data sensitivity, and discussion of block-size selection that acknowledges no Pareto-optimal prescription. It removes v1's model-size/kurtosis explanation for declining recovery.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies Brevitas v0.12.1 and use of its existing algorithm implementations. The reproducibility statement replaces the MixQuant repository-branch link with PeRQ documentation. Hardware and principal hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting GSM8K, C4, FineWeb, and the Brevitas release, while removing several citations, including FrameQuant, OSTQuant, and MagR. It sharpens the comparison with ZigZag; the central research positioning remains. GPTQ/OPTQ naming and publication updates refer to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the background and method exposition are rewritten or condensed. Computational discussion moves from Section 3.2 into Appendix A, Section 4 gains a separate MassDiff discussion, and the conclusion is reorganized. Framework naming, title, and headings also change throughout.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text to a two-column conference layout and redistributes existing displays. It adds Figure 5 and five tables, relocates the computational-cost table to Appendix A, corrects Figure 1's panel lettering, and revises Figure 4's colors and caption.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the unchanged method through the direct bound/error comparison, RTN controls, and calibration-sensitivity studies. Reporting inconsistencies temper these gains: Table 8 contradicts the claim of improvement on every task, with WikiText2-calibrated Winogrande accuracy falling from 53.1 to 51.0, and Table 10's claimed MR-Qronos control equivalence conflicts with Section 5's full-versus-block rotation settings. The independent additions nevertheless provide a positive overall improvement.
